sources.entry: DockSTARTer - DockSTARTer helps you get started with home server apps running in Docker. (Source Code) MIT Shell

summary.one_liner: DockSTARTer is a shell-based tool that helps you quickly set up and run home server apps in Docker.
summary.what_it_does: DockSTARTer is a Bash script tool whose stated goal is to make getting up and running with Docker quick and easy. Its README describes a one-time setup per platform that installs curl and git through the system package manager (APK, APT, DNF, Pacman, YUM, or Homebrew on macOS) and then runs its installer script. After a reboot, the user runs the `ds` command to open a main menu. From there, the Configuration menu offers a Full Setup that guides the user through selecting apps and starting containers. The README says it can be used directly for Docker system changes or as a stepping stone toward more advanced manual Docker configuration. It also describes an alternative install that clones the git repository manually instead of piping a script from the web.
use_cases: install home server apps in Docker
guided Docker app selection and container startup
set up a Docker host on Linux or macOS
learn Docker configuration step by step
how_to_run: Log in as a non-root user with sudo permissions
Install curl and git with your system package manager (for example: sudo apt-get install curl git)
Run the one-time install command for your distro from the README, then sudo reboot
In the main menu, select Configuration, then Full Setup
notable: Menu-driven ds command guides app selection and container startup
Supports multiple package managers: APK, APT, DNF, Pacman, YUM, and Homebrew
Documents a manual git clone install as a safer alternative to the piped install
Built on LinuxServer.io Docker images, per the README
caveats: Requires a supported platform and a non-root user with sudo permissions
macOS needs extra steps, including enabling Docker Desktop at sign-in and approving keychain permissions
The standard one-line install downloads a script using a method the README itself says carries known risks
